Subject: Dedicated capacity structure — need options and costs

Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. We liked Redwood's routing/fallback approach and want to scope dedicated capacity for a production rollout in H1. Procurement asked for a couple of discrete options for: cluster size, minimum guaranteed GPUs, ramp schedule tied to milestones, and an activation/cancellation cadence (esp. how burst credits and canary weeks work).

High level constraints:
- We expect peak qps for our inference paths to be ~2500 r/s during campaign spikes, average ~600 r/s.
- Latency SLO target is p95 < 220ms for the primary model.
- Compliance: data must be bounded to a dedicated pool and audit logs retained for 12 months.

Can you send a short menu (3-4 options) that map to expected unit economics and an onboarding timeline? Prefer a format procurement can review quickly.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Head of ML Infrastructure, CascadeWell

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity structure — need options and costs

Alicia — really appreciate the clear constraints. Attached is a short proposal + activation matrix (Attachment: CascadeWell_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf and Activation_Matrix_v2.xlsx). TL;DR below, three options that balance cost vs margin for burst tolerance and ramp speed: 

Option A — Starter Onramp (lower commit, faster start)
- Cluster target: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (single GPU type across the pool)
- Minimum guaranteed: 12 GPUs (soft floor)
- Burst windows: up to +50% for 72 hrs (consumes burst credits)
- Ramp schedule: month 0: 12 GPU live (canary), month 1: +6; month 2: +6 (reach 24)
- Expected throughput: ~600 r/s steady, ~1500 r/s short bursts with autoscale
- Pricing: lower monthly commit, higher overage

Option B — Balanced (recommended for steady growth)
- Cluster target: 48 GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed: 24 GPUs (hard floor with warm-start lanes)
- Burst windows: +60% sustained for 48 hrs (with pre-approved burst credits)
- Ramp schedule: week 0: 24 GPUs (canary + warm-up), week 4: +8, week 8: +8, week 12: +8 (reach 48)
- Expected throughput: ~1400 r/s steady, ~3000 r/s bursts with queued batching optimizations
- Pricing: mid commit, unit-cost improves after month 2

Option C — Anchored Slate (large reserved footprint for predictable peak)
- Cluster target: 80 GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed: 48 GPUs (hard floor)
- Burst windows: unlimited within reservation (no overage charges)
- Ramp schedule: phased activation over 10 weeks with parallel canaries and infra pre-warm at week -2
- Expected throughput: ~2500 r/s steady at peak; headroom for model upgrades
- Pricing: highest commit but lowest effective per-token cost and SLA SLA add-on available

Key gating items we recommend tying to ramp triggers (so you can reduce commit risk):
- Stage 1 (canary): internal acceptance tests + 7-day production smoke with p95 < 220ms
- Stage 2 (product ramp): sustained 30-day SLA adherence (latency + error budget)
- Stage 3 (full reservation): go/no-go based on 60-day burn and traffic forecasts

Marissa — I put in the initial financial bands in the PDF. Karthik, any infra caveats to call out for CascadeWell's p95 target?

If that looks ok I can format the three options into procurement-friendly one-pagers and hand off the DocuSign link for signatures.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake

Jordan / Alicia — quick engineering notes to make the options realistic for CascadeWell's workload: 

- Model characteristics: you mentioned medium-length contexts (~1k tokens) and mix of chat + reranking. We should recommend enabling KV cache pinning for sessions that have high reuse — this will effectively increase throughput by ~12-20% for the same GPU count.
- Option A: 24 GPUs will meet steady demand if you enable prefix caching and aggressive batching in the router, but the soft floor at 12 GPUs means any sustained burst beyond 1500 r/s will have higher latency until we spin up warm instances (8-12 hour warm-up depending on cold start strategy). Recommend increasing pre-warm concurrency if you have predictable campaign windows.
- Option B: Balanced is the practical sweet spot because the warm-start lanes prevent cold starts for the most common endpoints. For p95 < 220ms, target model quantization to int8 for the large transformer and keep critical endpoints on float16. We'll own kernel selection and tuning during onboarding.
- Option C: Anchored Slate: if CascadeWell needs headroom for A/B experiments and nightly retrains, 80 GPUs with a maintained 48-GPU floor is conservative but gives margin for model growth. If they want lower commit, we can introduce a staged overprovision buffer and longer burst-credit runway.

Operational suggestions:
- Canary weeks: 1 week with traffic mirroring, 1 week with live traffic at 10-25% (we track evals and regressions).
- Warm-up credits: we recommend 72 hours of warm-start credits included in month 0 for Options B & C to run pre-warm tasks.
- SLA add-on: 99.95% uptime on dedicated pools with network redundancy — requires zone-aware placement.

I'll attach a short ops checklist to the activation matrix. Jordan — happy for me to drop this into the spreadsheet before you send to procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Alicia — updated with Karthik's ops notes (see attached Activation_Matrix_v2.xlsx). Two quick clarifications before I convert Option B into a purchase-ready one-pager and a DocuSign packet: 

1) Minimum guaranteed semantics: do you need a contractual hard floor (billing guarantees even if unused) or would a soft floor + minimum monthly billing (credits that convert to rollover) be acceptable? Soft floor gives you cheaper entry with predictable protections.

2) Canary acceptance: do you have an internal metric owner who will sign the canary acceptance checklist (latency, error budget, and a small prompt-quality eval)? If so, please share their name / email so we can include them on the onboarding runbook.

If procurement prefers a fixed monthly number, Option B (48 GPUs) with the warm-start credits and a 30-day canary typically converts to a 12-month reserved pricing model with a mid-year true-up. I can have Marissa package the final numbers tomorrow and circulate.

Next steps:
- Alicia: confirm floor semantics & canary owner by EOD Wed 12/9
- Jordan (me) / Marissa: finalize one-pager and DocuSign packet by Thu 12/10
- Karthik: prep onboarding runbook and pre-warm checklist

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
